summary.text: 他 means “other; another” and is also used as the third-person pronoun “he, she, it.” A common analysis assigns 亻 the person category and proposes 也 as a sound element, though its historical role is disputed.

formation.text: The construction of 他 is unresolved. A common account analyzes it as 亻, contributing the person category, plus 也 as a proposed sound element, but the supplied historical readings do not establish that phonetic role. A separate traditional account analyzes 佗 as 人 plus phonetic 它 and links 佗 with 他; it does not establish that construction for 他.

components.text: 亻 is the conventional side form of 人 and contributes the person category in the common analysis of 他. 人 is also assigned that role in the reported analysis of the separate graph 佗.

也 is commonly proposed as the phonetic element in 他, but that role remains disputed. The supplied historical readings differ, and their current Mandarin readings do not establish an ancient sound relationship.

sound_limitation.text: The historical comparison and current Mandarin readings do not establish that 也 functioned as 他’s historical phonetic element; the structural analysis remains disputed.

sound.text: In the supplied table, 也 is MC yaeX / OC *lAjʔ and 他 is MC tha / OC *l̥ˤaj; these readings differ and do not establish 也’s phonetic role.

sound.text: The supplied current Mandarin readings are 也 yě and 他 tā. This records their present pronunciations, not a historical sound relationship.

components.text: In the reported analysis of 佗, 人 contributes the person category. This component belongs to 佗’s analysis, not to an established earlier breakdown of 他.
In the reported analysis of 佗, 它 supplies the sound cue. The supplied Baxter–Sagart table gives 它 and 佗 matching readings, but those readings do not independently establish 它’s phonetic role in 佗.

sound_limitation.text: The matching historical readings and current Mandarin pair support sound comparison but do not independently prove 佗’s graphic analysis or its later relation to 他.

history.text: Traditional dictionary accounts analyze 佗 as 人 plus phonetic 它 and report that it was used for 他. One account describes 他 as a clerical transformation of 佗; a secondary form-history account instead proposes an earlier right-side 它 changing to 也 in clerical script. No verified form sequence settles how these accounts relate.
Transmitted 詩經 and 孟子 passages use 他 for “other” or “else.” These citations do not date the graph’s first use or establish when its third-person use arose.

uncertainties.text: The accounts link 佗 and 他 but differ on their graphic history. They do not establish whether 也 was an original phonetic element in 他.
Both “other/else” and third-person uses are supported, but their earliest attestations, the date the pronoun use arose, and a semantic bridge between them remain unresolved.

senses.text: Transmitted 詩經 and 孟子 passages use 他 for “other/else”; they do not date the first use of the graph.
他 is also used as a third-person pronoun. Its earliest attestation and the date this use arose are unresolved.

limitations.text: The evidence does not establish that third-person 他 developed from “other/else,” or date its emergence. A claimed post-Han emergence and displacement of earlier pronouns remains unverified.

overview.text: 他 means “other; another” and also serves as the third-person pronoun “he, she, it.” A common analysis assigns 亻 the person category and proposes 也 as a disputed sound element.

In 佗, 它 is reported as the sound element. The supplied Mandarin readings are 它 tā and 佗 tuó; this comparison and the reported link to 他 do not establish 它’s role in 他.

takeaway.text: Later dictionary accounts link 他 with 佗, but the precise graphic history remains unresolved.

relationships.text: 亻 is commonly analyzed as the person-category component of 他.
A common structural analysis assigns 也 a phonetic role, but the supplied historical readings do not establish a close match or prove that role.
Dictionary accounts report 佗 as used for 他 and describe 他 as a later form, without fixing the date or precise graphic mechanism.
